body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
On every realized sample for which all selected Gram matrices pass and the cohortwise minimizers exist, profiling the event coefficient gives
\[
\widehat\theta_s=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s.
\]
The event term then has no \(\gamma\)-dependent component, \(\widehat\gamma_s\) is exactly the historical local-polynomial fit in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}, and \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}=\widehat\tau\) exactly.
body.justification: This result ties the statistical regression target to a causal level-wealth estimand and to the implementable full-donor panel coefficient.
body.gap: The path-conditioned transport relation identifies compounded wealth rather than defining it through a generated benchmark.
body.consumer: Applied event studies obtain a declared coefficient and causal estimand from one cohort fit centered at the full donor mean.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr E=\sigma(E_0)\).  By the definition of \(z_0\), the vector \(z_0=\mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid E_0]\) is \(\mathscr E\)-measurable.  Thus adjoining \(z_0\) to the conditioning field generated by \(E_0\) does not change any conditional expectation below.  By \texttt{def:target} and linearity of conditional expectation,
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]
-\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} and the definition of \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) give
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0].
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-transport} gives, for each cohort,
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=m_s(z_{0s}).
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (2)--(3) into (1) proves
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-regression} identifies \(m_s(x)\) separately as the observed-law conditional mean of an untreated pseudo-event response at \(X_{st}=x\).  Hence consistency and event transport prove the equality between the causal contrast and the observed-law functional; it is not introduced as a definition of the causal target.

Fix a successful cohort \(s\), abbreviate \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by \(\bar B_s\), and hold \(\gamma\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\) fixed.  The event part of the criterion in \texttt{def:fwl-regression} satisfies the exact sum-of-squares identity
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\theta-e_0^\top\gamma)^2
=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_s)^2
+(\bar B_s-\theta-e_0^\top\gamma)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently, for fixed \(\gamma\), the unique minimizing event coefficient is
\[
\theta=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\gamma.
\tag{5}
\]
At (5), the event criterion is independent of \(\gamma\).  Up to the first, constant term in (4), the profiled criterion is therefore
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{st})^\top\gamma\}^2,
\tag{6}
\]
which is precisely the historical weighted least-squares problem in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  Passage of the normalized-shape test implies \(L_s>0\) and
\[
G_s\succeq c_GL_sI_{q_r}\succ0.
\]
Thus (6) has the unique minimizer \(\widehat\gamma_s\), and profiling gives
\[
\widehat\theta_s=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s.
\tag{7}
\]
Using the definitions of \(\widehat m_s\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}\), and \(\widehat\tau\), on every sample for which all selected fits exist,
\[
\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s)
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)
=\widehat\tau.
\]
